answer:
Historians don't agree on one single cause. Most say several problems built on each other until the Western Empire collapsed in 476 [1][2]. Here are the main reasons:

1. Political instability: frequent coups, civil wars and short-lived or weak emperors, which were worst during the crisis of the third century [1][2].
2. Economic trouble: heavy taxes, inflation from debased coins, costly wars and shrinking trade, plus a widening gap between rich and poor [1][2].
3. Military weakness: the army relied more and more on Germanic soldiers and allies whose loyalty was uncertain [2].
4. Outside pressure and invasions: the Goths, Vandals and Huns pushed on the borders, and the Visigoths sacked Rome in 410 [2].
5. The split into East and West: the richer Eastern Empire survived until 1453, while the poorer West was left to defend itself [1][2].
6. Disease and climate: some historians also point to epidemics and droughts as contributing factors [3].
